title: Reality Fracture Limited Set Reviews
scale: 0-5 numeric scale (5.0 best in set, 3.0-3.5 good commons, 4.0+ good rares); ranges or split grades given for build-arounds, sideboard cards and Draft vs Sealed

format.summary: A Jace-token-heavy format where many cards Empower Jace, creating planeswalkers to protect and attack, alongside prepared creatures, landcyclers, surveil, Heartwood tokens, self-mill/threshold, lifegain and ten two-color archetypes; LSV calls it sweet with lots of themes and fantastic cards, and Uldaros Theorix his pick for best card.
format.speed: Martin expects the format to be on the slower side, especially Sealed, making expensive bombs, grindy value and late-game threats better; Draft is expected to be faster than Sealed.

colors.take: Martin thinks white is good, with four removal spells that each need just one white pip, making it popular and splashable in Sealed.
LSV thinks blue is doing well, combining card advantage and speed with strong commons like Mindseeker Oculus and Infinite Coursework.
LSV rates black's commons awesome, with good removal, a strong landcycler and solid creatures, though its creatures skew small.
Martin likes red's efficient removal but notes many cards only work in one or two pairs, and aggro/prowess cards are weaker in Sealed.
Martin thinks green is very strong with ramp, synergy, mana sinks, fight removal and big late threats, despite several unplayable cards.

pairs.take: Lifegain and +1/+1 counters archetype with payoffs like Bloombrute, Titanbones, Way of the Mentor and Vigorbloom Vanguard.
Surveil and fliers deck using Peer Review cards, with Denzilore Fatehold, Codie and Eye of Jace as payoffs.
Self-mill and threshold archetype, supported by Liliana the Repentant, Paradox Shaper, Recursive Recruitment and Uldaros Theorix.
Prowess and cheap-spells deck with Pompous Battlemage, Chandra's Emberling and Frostbite Pyromental.
Stingerquill deal-one-damage and Viscous Verse deck, fueled by Stingerquill Voxmancer, Tomik and Koth, the Geomancer.
Heartwood token ramp deck with big payoffs like Craftwork Crusher, Karn, Gilded Guardian and Draconic Visitor.
Aggressive go-wide and +1/+1 counters deck with Warrior's Blades, Mabel and Winter, Team Player.
Graveyard recursion and self-mill deck where Tarmogoyf, Carnivorous Cultivator and Restore with Empathy shine.
Creature-heavy sacrifice deck supported by Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord.
Planeswalker-focused deck, likely where Inspired Tethermage and Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes are best.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace / Jace tokens
mechanics.take: Pervasive planeswalker tokens that reward cheap evasive attackers, cast spells before attacking so you can hit their Jace, and power up Way enchantments and Jace payoffs.

mechanics.name: Prepared creatures (Seed Suture, Peer Review, Viscous Verse, Molten Tide)
mechanics.take: Creatures that come with cheap spells, providing value, lifegain triggers, prowess triggers and targeting for your own creatures.

mechanics.name: Landcycling
mechanics.take: Makes big creatures like Apex Witchstalker and Undulating Witness flexible and very playable.

mechanics.name: Surveil
mechanics.take: Common via Jace tokens, enabling graveyard synergies and payoffs like Saheeli, Consul of Oversight and Proctor of Potential.

mechanics.name: Heartwood tokens
mechanics.take: Ramp and fuel for Red-Green payoffs and mana sinks, though too many extra mana sources risk flooding.

mechanics.name: Threshold / self-mill (Omit Variables)
mechanics.take: Feast-or-famine cards that are great only when going hard on the theme.

mechanics.name: Color hosers
mechanics.take: A cycle of color-specific cards that are excellent sideboard options but not mainboard material.

advice: Prioritize cheap removal like Last Gasp, Extended Absence, No Admittance and Compel Brutality.
Draft cheap evasive creatures and menace to pressure opposing Jace tokens while protecting yours.
Value landcyclers and multi-purpose cards; play multiple Apex Witchstalkers or Mindseeker Oculuses happily.
Don't auto-play rares like Flickering Hound or Liliana the Faultless without the synergy they need.
Expensive bombs and grindy cards gain value in Sealed, which is slower than Draft.
Treat build-arounds (self-mill, sacrifice, Heartwood) as feast or famine and only play them when committed.
If you open Splinter Twin, pair it with the common Divining Duelist for an infinite combo.
Common and rare dual lands are strong picks that enable multicolor decks and splashes.
